competitors.name: Huawei Investment & Holding Co., Ltd.
competitors.why: Named by VRT 10-K Item 1/1A as a large-scale global competitor competing directly; Huawei Digital Power sells UPS and prefabricated modular data centers, mainly in China/APAC, Middle East and Africa (VRT APAC and EMEA).

bottlenecks.reading: Demand for VRT's power and thermal equipment runs well ahead of its deliveries: Q4 2025 organic orders +~252% y/y, book-to-bill ~2.9x, backlog $15.0bn at 2025-12-31 (+109% y/y), more than 1x the 2026 sales guidance midpoint of $14.0bn. Q3 2026 organic sales guide 34-36%.

VRT is adding its own capacity: it more than doubled switchgear, busbar and integrated power manufacturing capacity since late 2021; 2026 capex guided to $550-570m (raised from $425-525m in the 10-K) vs $226.4m in 2025; Q2 2026 sales were held back by 'temporary supply chain congestion and multi-phased project execution'. The binding constraint is factory output and supply chain, not demand.

Paid pricing power in VRT's own numbers: Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin 22.6%, +410 bp y/y, attributed by the company to productivity and favorable price-cost including tariff countermeasures; Q3 2026 guide 24.0-25.0%.

The shortage is shared and competitors are also scaling: Eaton Electrical Global backlog +103% and Electrical Americas backlog +33% y/y at June 2026 with Electrical Americas margin 27.5%; Schneider reports triple-digit data-center demand growth and a record backlog in Q3 2026; Legrand data centers 32% of sales, organic >30% in H1 2026; Delta revenue +48% in Q2 2026 with data center >50% of revenue. Capacity is being added by every named supplier, so the scarcity premium is not VRT's alone.

Market direction: the IEA (Energy and AI, April 2025) projects global data-centre electricity demand to more than double to ~945 TWh by 2030 (from ~415 TWh in 2024), with AI-optimised data-centre demand more than quadrupling and data centres almost half of US electricity demand growth to 2030. Power and cooling equipment per MW scales with this build-out (search excerpt, not the report itself).

How long the shortage lasts: it lasts while hyperscaler/AI capex keeps growing faster than the combined capacity additions of VRT, Eaton, Schneider, Legrand and Delta; a capex pause or a catch-up of supplier capacity (all five are expanding) would turn backlog into price competition. No dated supply/demand balance from an attributed study was retrieved.

Rising rack power density (AI racks) shifts content toward liquid cooling and higher-voltage power distribution, where VRT, Schneider (Motivair), Eaton (Boyd Thermal) and Delta all compete; the technology shift is both VRT's opportunity and the entry path for competitors that bought liquid-cooling capacity in 2025-26.

notes: fd NAMED COMPETITORS (10-K Item 1, pf_10k_20260213): large-scale global: Schneider Electric S.E., Eaton Corporation plc, Legrand SA, Huawei Investment & Holding Co., Ltd.; regional/product: Delta Electronics, Stulz GmbH, Johnson Controls International plc, Socomec Holding SA. Item 1A repeats that Schneider, Eaton, Legrand and Huawei compete directly in the markets in which VRT operates. No competitor added beyond the company's own list.

fd SHARE Americas, same quarter Q2 2026: VRT Americas net sales $2,070.8m, +29.2% reported, +21.1% organic (pf_rel_20260729_1) vs Eaton Electrical Americas $4.0bn, +18% organic (fd_etn_q2_2026): VRT grew slightly faster than the closest named competitor segment; Eaton's segment includes non-data-center end markets, so this is not a clean data-center share reading.

fd SHARE total, Q2 2026 / H1 2026: VRT organic +18% in Q2 2026 (pf_rel_20260729_1) vs Delta revenue +48% (fd_delta_2q26), Legrand data-center organic >30% in H1 (fd_lr_h1_2026) and Schneider data-center demand up triple digits in Q3 (fd_su_q3_2026): on Q2 revenue VRT did NOT outgrow the data-center businesses of Delta and Legrand; VRT's own explanation is supply-chain congestion and project phasing (pf_rel_20260729_1), and its Q3 organic guide is 34-36%. Reading: share is being contested; Q3 2026 actuals (released 2026-10-28) decide whether Q2 was timing.

fd SHARE EMEA: VRT EMEA net sales H1 2026 $805.0m, -8.4% y/y (Q2 +1.7%) (pf_rel_20260729_1) while Schneider Europe grew +8.6% organic in Q3 2026 (fd_su_q3_2026, different quarter) and Legrand grew organically +9.8% group-wide in H1: VRT is losing share in EMEA on these numbers (periods not perfectly aligned).

fd SHARE orders: VRT backlog +109% y/y at 2025-12-31 (pf_rel_20260211_1) vs Eaton Electrical Americas backlog +33% and Electrical Global +103% y/y at 2026-06-30 (fd_etn_q2_2026): VRT's order intake outgrew Eaton's Americas segment; periods differ by two quarters.

fd MARGINS vs competitors: VRT Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin 22.6% (pf_rel_20260729_1) vs Eaton Electrical Americas 27.5% and Electrical Global 19.8% segment margin, Legrand adjusted operating margin 20.8% (H1), Delta operating margin 16.7% (Q2): VRT's margin is inside the competitor range, below Eaton's Americas segment.
